standard_prerequisites.name: Absolutely flat rings: reduced, with every local ring a field
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives reducedness of B and the field property of its local rings, which the rest of the argument uses.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weakly etale maps and their composition, and weakly etale fields as separable algebraic extensions
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the hypothesis into the separability of the residue field extensions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dimension-zero rings as products of their local rings, and etale algebras over a field as reduced rings with finite separable residue fields
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the criterion that turns the dimension-zero conclusion into etaleness of A over K.

core_obligations: Record that (1) and (2) are equivalent because every K-algebra is flat over K, and that (3) implies (1) and (2) by the weakly etale lemma (proof lines 30517-30518).
Assume (1) and (2) and deduce that B is absolutely flat, using that a field is absolutely flat; conclude that B is reduced and that every local ring of B is a field (proof lines 30521-30525).
For a prime q of B, note that B -> B_q is weakly etale, hence B_q is weakly etale over K, and therefore B_q is a separable algebraic extension of K (proof lines 30528-30532).

For a finitely generated K-subalgebra A of B, show every minimal prime p of A is the image of a prime q of B, so that kappa(p), viewed as a subfield of B_q = kappa(q), is separable algebraic over K (proof lines 30535-30542).
Conclude that every generic point of Spec(A) is closed, hence dim(A) = 0 (proof lines 30543-30545).

Use that a zero-dimensional ring is the product of its local rings, and that since A is reduced those local rings equal their residue fields, which are finite separable over K, to conclude that A is etale over K; this proves both (3) and the finite statement (proof lines 30546-30552).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a K-algebra B over a field K and gives three equivalent conditions: that the multiplication B tensor_K B -> B be flat; that K -> B be weakly etale; and that B be a filtered colimit of etale K-algebras; it adds that every finitely generated K-subalgebra of B is etale over K (source lines 30503-30514). The equivalence of (1) and (2) is immediate because every K-algebra is flat over K, and (3) implies (1) and (2) is the direction supplied by an earlier lemma, so the substance is the converse. Assuming (1) and (2), the proof first notes that a field is absolutely flat, hence B is an absolutely flat ring, so B is reduced and every local ring of B is a field (proof lines 30521-30525). It then takes a prime q of B, observes that B -> B_q is weakly etale so that B_q is weakly etale over K, and concludes that B_q is a separable algebraic extension of K (proof lines 30528-30532). The final step is the substantive one: for a finitely generated K-subalgebra A of B, every minimal prime p of A is the image of a prime q of B, so kappa(p) viewed inside B_q = kappa(q) is separable algebraic over K; hence every generic point of Spec(A) is closed, so dim(A) = 0, so A is the product of its local rings, and since A is reduced those local rings equal their residue fields, which are finite separable over K, so A is etale over K (proof lines 30535-30552). The non-routine content is the dimension-zero argument together with the identification of the finite etale algebras over a field as reduced zero-dimensional rings with finite separable residue fields.
